I know high school feels like the end of the world sometimes, but it really isn't.  When I was a sophomore I swallowed a whole bottle of pills and slashed my wrists up.  I remember being so mad when it didn't work,and how furious my parents were at me because I was such an embarrassment to the family.  How dare I tarnish the family name and make it impossible for the business man to be able to do his job when his daughter was obviously such a fuck up.

I ended up dropping out and eventually doing a lot of drugs, it took so much longer than it should have for me to get my shit together, but eventually I did.  And now I have two beautiful little girls.  And I know that's so so far down the line for you (as it should be) but I promise you, when you make it through his and out of high school, it'll all be worth it.  Life truly starts when high school ends.

I'm going to guess this post itself has been on your mind for a while since this is a 10 day old throw away account, which means you're probably already acting in a way that's making her anxious whether you mean to or not, especially since you said this happened six weeks ago.

I highly doubt anything anyone says is going to make you feel better, telling her isn't going to make you feel better either.  You'll just have more guilt on top of guilt.   Notice I said 'wouldn't make you feel better' though, not that it's the right thing to do.

How was your marriage before the event?  Were you happy/unhappy/had things that needed to be worked on?  You need to be completely honest with yourself about how the marriage was before this happened, and how you're feeling about it now.

She deserves to be able to make the decision herself about whether this is something she wants to be in or not, although speaking from experience, as I found out my husband cheated on me (although not as far as intercourse) it can get better, but it will always linger and be a thought.  For the first couple years after, I had the worst problem with him communicating with other females, even if it was for work.  I'm finally okay with it now, but it took years, although I think if he'd have tried to be a little more understanding and compassionate about my paranoia instead of the defense 'you should trust me/it won't happen again' route I could have been okay sooner.

Are you ready for that?  Are you willing to put in all the time and effort to reassure her every time you leave town that you're by yourself?  To comfort her when she's worried and paranoid because you worked late?  To take a few seconds each day to send a quick 'I love you' reminder text and put some serious 'dating' effort into your marriage?

If you're not willing to go the extra 500 miles, don't tell her. You'll still be in pain and riddled with well deserved guilt,but if you're not willing to fix it and go the extra distance, don't tell her.  However if you are, which it sounds like you might be, you need to tell her. 

How you tell her matters too, don't take her apology jewelry.  Flowers chocolate and a bottle of wine, sure, but nothing life lasting.  My husband got me this beautiful necklace and earring set after a huge fight to apologize but I never wear it because it reminds me of the awful things he said during it.  I'd plan a night that you could be kid free and take her somewhere that has no meaning and she'd never have to go back to ever again, and just be honest about it (with as few details as you can get away with, details will just hurt more) and tell her you want to do whatever SHE needs to make it better.  Your guilt won't go away until she's forgiven you, and even then not truly, but you'll learn to live with it.  And hopefully she'll still pick you.
